candidates.name: St. John's Co Cathedral
candidates.price: €15 for adults (includes an audio guide) — buy online to skip the queue for tickets
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 09:00-16:45, last entry 16:15; closed Sun and holidays
candidates.content: Unremarkable from the outside, but incredibly ornate on the inside. Each of the different 'langues' (knights of a particular nationality had their own langue) has its own chapel lined along the side of the nave in which they tried

candidates.name: Palace of the Grand Masters
candidates.hours: Jan Feb: daily 09:00-17:00; Mar-Dec: daily 10:00-18:00; (armoury sometimes closed for functions)
candidates.content: Now it is the President's office and the Maltese parliament. The staterooms, when accessible, are quite impressive. It also houses the Knights' armoury, which is open to visitors daily from 09:00-17:00. (However, all other parts o

candidates.name: The National Museum of Archaeology
candidates.content: Even though Malta has an impressive and unique ancient history, this museum, housed in the former Auberge de Provence in Republic Street can be rather a disappointment. The museum is partially being renovated, hopefully bringing s

candidates.name: Fort St. Elmo
candidates.content: Built at the tip of the peninsula by the knights after the Dragut Raid of 1551. During the Great Siege of 1565 the Turks made the mistake of choosing to first take this fort, for which they had planned a week. Instead, the knights

candidates.name: Hal Saflieni Hypogeum
candidates.price: €35 in advance (€20 for seniors 60+), €50 for "last minute" tickets, if available
candidates.hours: Eight tours are conducted daily, starting on the hour from 09:00 till 16:00 (last tour)
candidates.content: The Hal Saflieni Hypogeum is a subterranean structure excavated c. 2500 BC. Thought to have been built as a sanctuary, it became a necropolis in prehistoric times. It is the only prehistoric underground temple in the world. To ens

candidates.name: The National Library
candidates.content: An evocative old library on Republic Square, next to the Grandmaster's Palace. Only part of it is open to the public: you will need to take a passport or other photo ID to get in. The entire archives of the Knights of St. John fro

candidates.name: Malta Postal Museum
candidates.content: Museum run by Maltapost, including a working post office.

candidates.name: The Casa Rocca Piccola
candidates.content: A Maltese noble family house on Triq ir-Republika, a few hundred metres past the Grand Master's Palace on the right-hand side. Very enjoyable.

candidates.name: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral
candidates.content: Anglican cathedral built in 1844, with memorials to the World War 2 defence of Malta.

candidates.name: Belfrey Tour
candidates.content: takes you to a spectacular view of the cathedral from the gallery, and then up to the roof for okay views of the city. Timed tickets are available only at the cathedral; enquire when you go in.

candidates.name: The Sacra Infermeria
candidates.content: The great hospital built by the knights in the 16th century was a hospital with the highest level of healthcare available in Europe at the time for men, both rich and poor, with non-contagious diseases (contagious disease patients

candidates.name: St. James Cavalier
candidates.content: A fortress opposite the Auberge of Castille (today the Prime Minister's office) which was built as part of the elaborate defence systems of Valletta. Today it houses a 'Centre for Creativity', with its own theatre, cinema, music r

candidates.name: Tarxien Temples
candidates.content: This site, dating from 3600 to 2500 BC, is the most complex of all temple sites in Malta and consists of four megalithic structures.

candidates.name: Lascaris War Rooms
candidates.price: Adult (16+) €20, senior €19, family (2 adults & 3 children under 16) €35, child (5-15) €7
candidates.content: Underground complex which was used as the British HQ during the defence of Malta in World War II.

candidates.name: City Gate
candidates.content: The fifth incarnation of the main entrance to the city was built between 2011 and 2014 to design of the Italian architect Renzo Piano. The first gate on this site was built in 1569.

candidates.name: Parliament House
candidates.content: Malta Parliament building built between 2011 and 2015 at a cost of €90 million to a design by Renzo Piano. The building's design of two large stone blocks on stilts is controversial, but it has low emissions with solar panels on t

candidates.name: Spinola Palace
candidates.content: Built in the 17th century by Fra Paolo Rafel Spinola, a knight of the Order of St. John.

candidates.name: The Upper Barrakka Gardens
candidates.content: The gardens offer a jaw-dropping view of the Grand Harbour. Go on a sunny day and bring champagne!

candidates.name: Fortifications of Valletta
candidates.content: The imposing defence walls and ramparts at the entrance to Valletta, built by the Knights in the late 16th century are interesting to explore.

candidates.name: Saint George's Tower
candidates.content: A small watchtower. It's part of the Lascaris towers, a series of watchtowers constructed by the Order of Saint John between 1637 and 1652. Notice that the tower is located on the grounds of a hotel.

candidates.name: Works by Caravaggio
candidates.content: Holds two works by Caravaggio, who was briefly himself a knight: the first one is the huge "Beheading of St. John the Baptist" (do not miss the explanatory light show up the staircase on your right), and the more modest Saint Jero

candidates.name: The Malta Experience
candidates.price: Adult €20, student with ID €15.50, child 5 - 11 years old €9
candidates.content: Despite not being cheap, visitors who have any interest in culture or history and who haven't exhaustively read up on the country before coming here would do well by starting their visit to Malta by going here, as it is an excelle

candidates.name: Chapel of the Immaculate Conception
candidates.content: Roman Catholic chapel built in 1687.

candidates.name: Saluting Battery
candidates.content: A gun is fired twice a day M-Sa, at 12:00 and 16:00.

candidates.name: Manoel Theatre
candidates.content: 'La Scala' in miniature, a very beautiful 17th-century theatre in its original state. One of the oldest active theaters in Europe, it is the place for many classical music performances but also for instance the hilarious Christmas

candidates.name: Pjazza Teatru Rjal
candidates.content: Open theatre on the site of the former Royal Opera House which was destroyed by a bomb in 1942. The outdoor theatre was designed by Renzo Piano and opened in 2013.

candidates.name: Valletta International Baroque Festival
candidates.content: Festival of baroque music concerts and operas.

candidates.name: Coastal Walk
candidates.content: You can take a spectacular walk along the sea around the outside of the city walls. If you go to the mooring place where the ferry for Sliema leaves, there is the possibility to walk over the rocks towards the tip of the peninsula

candidates.name: Dragonara Palace
candidates.content: Built in 1870, and now a casino.

candidates.name: St. George's Square
candidates.content: At night in St George's Square, there is a lovely water fountain, with coloured spouts of water which pop up and down - a fantastic play opportunity for children. They will get wet, so don't let them go near if they are wearing th

candidates.name: Audio Guide
candidates.content: To get further historical information about the numerous places of interest in Valletta it can be useful to get an audio guide. It is available in different languages from the Archeology Museum on Republic Street. You can choose i

candidates.name: Malta Blue Diving
candidates.content: Small family-run dive shop with new equipment, flexible diving schedules and friendly staff. They teach PADI diving courses in small groups in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere and plan diving to customers requirements and diving

candidates.name: Trabuxu Wine Bar
candidates.content: A charming wine bar in an ancient cellar serving light meals. It's at the beginning of a small alley parallel to Republic street, look for the wooden sign with the corkscrew. The bistro is opposite, on South Street.

candidates.name: Rampila Restaurant and Wine bar
candidates.content: Maltese-Mediterranean fusion restaurant and wine bar in the impressive bastions. You can enjoy a fine plate of fresh seafood, meat, game, pasta or risotto there or enjoy a platter and/or dips accompanied by wine from an extensive

candidates.name: The Pub
candidates.content: A place where actor Oliver Reed died in a drinking match against a group of sailors.

candidates.name: Cafe Society
candidates.content: The only queer bar in Malta. Great drinks. Guests spill out into the street in warmer months.

candidates.name: Legligin
candidates.content: A set menu of Maltese dishes. Food varies each day depending on what they buy at market. Vegetarian options. No à la carte menu. Wine pairing for €40 extra.

candidates.name: Croce Bonaci Caterers
candidates.content: Secluded site with wery good breakfast and tremendous sandwiches. Great little café with friendly and helpful staff. Authentic Maltese food. Excellent welcome.

candidates.name: Museum Cafe
candidates.content: Cosy little café with very impressive interior and amazing food. It is one of the old Maltese bars as they ought to be. Great to enjoy original Maltese ftira. The owner is super nice and accommodating.

candidates.name: Nenu the Artisan Baker
candidates.content: Bakery famous for its ftira (traditional Maltese ring-formed bread). Also serves Maltese dishes and desserts.

candidates.name: No.43
candidates.content: Café with fresh sandwiches, soups, salads and home made cakes. At the counter you can choose salads to eat in or take out.

candidates.name: The Submarine
candidates.content: Kind and good sandwiches. The Porchetta is sublime. Most humble ftira and salads in the city. Vegan and Vegetarian friendly.

candidates.name: Old Bakery's Pizza e Pasta
candidates.content: Small size pizza restaurant. Fresh ingredients for a good pizza cooked in a wood oven. The pizza is tasteful like Italian pizzas.

candidates.name: The Circle's Bar And Coffe Shop
candidates.content: The interior is charming and the food is homely. A great air-conditioned place to have a break from the sun.

candidates.name: Da' Pippo Trattoria
candidates.content: A place where locals go for lunch. Good seafood.

candidates.name: Rubino
candidates.content: Maltese traditional cuisine is served in this restaurant which was opened in 1906. Prior reservation recommended.

candidates.name: Café Deux Baronnes
candidates.content: Expensive even by local standards, but the cafe has a relaxed atmosphere and a good view of Grand Harbour and Fort Sant'Angelo.

candidates.name: Sliema Wanderers
candidates.content: Venue also has a nice ambience away from the hussle and bustle of sea front. The best tuna ftira in Sliema and wonderful atmosphere, thanks to the owners. Highly recommended for any kind of meal.

candidates.name: Farmers Market
candidates.content: Every Sunday there's a market in front of St. James Cavalier, with local food products and textiles.

candidates.name: Fish Market
candidates.content: Every morning, you can buy fresh fish next to the Castillan Curtains.

Manoel Theatre: 'La Scala' in miniature, a very beautiful 17th-century theatre in its original state. One of the oldest active theaters in Europe, it is the place for many classical music performances but also for instance the hilarious Christmas Panto.

Agenda Bookshop: The best bookshop in Malta is definitely the one formerly known as Sapienzas on Republic Street, but can be a bit more expensive. There is another branch near The Embassy Hotel on St. Lucia Street.
Luciano Restaurant: Good food for reasonable prices in a charming location near cathedral - big portions. On 3rd floor of Luciano Hotel.
